thread:
maya: Brain-dump / quick check: I prototyped a 'spillover' flow for prefix cache pressure. Idea: instead of evicting aggressively into oblivion, move cold prefixes to a local spill queue on SSD with a light tombstone in-memory. This gives us cheaper rehydrate (local disk) and a clear signal to readers that the prefix is demoted but recoverable.

jon: Interesting. How is this different from current prefill/repopulate logic? Concerned about rehydrate storms and disk IO amplification.

maya: Good point. Differences: (1) spill is eviction-first action when memory high, (2) rehydrate is strictly background and rate-limited, (3) spill tombstone carries a lease-epoch and a spill-seq so the handoff path can reason about ownership and avoid double-apply.

priya: +1 on the sequenced tombstone. Also recommend: when we enqueue to spill queue we emit an admission token to the lease manager: `spill_claim:{tenant,epoch,seq}`. Any node that tries to rehydrate must validate the token against the current lease epoch to prevent resurrecting stale data.

tom: Implementation constraints: we need a tiny on-disk segmenter per shard (append-only files) and a compactor. On rehydrate we stream only needed keys back into memory rather than whole prefix. That keeps IO low. We'll expose knobs: spill_threshold_pct, spill_batch_size, rehydrate_concurrency.

priya: Observability: track spill_enqueue_rate, spill_dequeue_rate, spill_backlog_len, rehydrate_throttle_count, rehydrate_latency_p50/p99. Add an alert when spill_backlog_len > X for > 2m.

infra-bot: Note: disk-backed spillers will trigger extra ops SLO considerations. Please add opt-in flag for Dedicated vs Hosted clusters.

jon: Failure modes: what if a node crashes and spill files are lost? How do we ensure we don't have invisible data loss?

maya: Recovery plan: tombstone metadata is replicated to the metadata store (small record, <1KB) before acknowledging eviction. On restart, if local spill files are missing but tombstone exists, rehydrate will fetch from peer/remote and repair. If both missing we surface a recoverability incident for the tenant.

priya: That approach keeps the hot-path cheap but requires a durable tiny write. Acceptable tradeoff. Also, add protective measure: don't consider prefix fully evicted until tombstone replicated (two-phase ack).

tom: Perf test idea: run a mixed-tenant synthetic with low/high QoS, force memory pressure and disk failure injected mid-run. Measure eviction correctness, rehydrate storm, and tail latencies.

jon: Also simulate frequent handoffs: migrate tenant ownership every 10s to test token/epoch validation.

maya: UX/API: keep it internal. Operator knobs only; no user-visible API. For Dedicated we can expose the spill tuning in Console.

priya: Action items: 1) maya: push POC spillage writer/reader (EOW). 2) tom: sketch on-disk layout + compactor (3d). 3) jon: test harness scenarios + chaos plan (2w). 4) I'll add metrics and canary alert thresholds.

infra-bot: Canary flag created: feature/spillover-cache -> staging. Owner: maya.

maya: Thanks everyone. If we see rehydrate storms we fall back to pure in-memory eviction and escalate. Will update once POC lands. :thumbsup:
